name: Nanyang Technological University
description: Nanyang Technological University is a public research university established in 1991, with roots in Nanyang University (1955) and the Nanyang Technological Institute (1981). Based on a campus in western Singapore, it is known for engineering, science and business, and jointly runs the Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine with Imperial College London.
whyIncluded: One of Singapore's Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded Autonomous Universities and, with NUS, one of the two comprehensive local universities that most Singaporean students weigh against overseas options.

programmes.name: MSc (School of EEE self-financed coursework programme, e.g. MSc Communications Engineering)
programmes.summary: Total tuition for the one-year programme, including 9% GST. Citizen/PR figure is the international fee less a S$5,000 subsidy NTU has not confirmed for this intake, so check before relying on it. Miscellaneous fees extra.
programmes.notes: Self-financed programme; the page states students are not eligible for MOE subsidies. Minimum total tuition (30 AUs) incl. 9% GST for admission in AY2027 (from Aug 2027): S$58,403.07; AY2026: S$56,156.80. Published as one figure for all nationalities, so the international tier is the fee everyone pays (incl. 9% GST). No current Citizen/PR tier (re-checked 2026-10-02): the page's 'SC/SPR Incentive' and 'MSc Programme Financial Support' sections, the NTU Graduate Admissions financial-matters page (/admissions/graduate/financialmatters/ntupgi) and coursework admission guide (/admissions/graduate/cwadmissionguide), the School's MSc brochure PDF and the EEE MSc FAQ state the S$5,000 NTU subsidy for Singaporeans/PRs in self-financed master's by coursework programmes only 'from the academic year starting in 2024' and 'for academic year starting in 2025'; no NTU statement was found that it continues for the AY2026/27 or AY2027/28 intakes, so no SC/PR fee is derived for those intakes. History: the AY2025 intake total is from the Wayback Machine capture of this page dated 2 Jun 2025 (web.archive.org timestamp 20250602151144), which states 'From August 2025 Intake Onwards ... Minimum Total Tuition Fees (30 AUs): SGD$56,156.80' incl. GST and, on the same page, that the S$5,000 SC/PR subsidy applies for the academic year starting in 2025; the 2025 citizen and pr rows are DERIVED as S$56,156.80 - S$5,000 = S$51,156.80 (deducted from the GST-inclusive total; the page does not say whether it is applied before GST). AY2024 intake: no source states the 2024 total, so no 2024 rows are recorded. The earliest archived capture of the financial-matters page is the June 2025 one above; 2024 captures of the EEE MSc landing page, FAQ and NTU's central programme pages could not be retrieved (the current versions link to the financial-matters page rather than quoting fees), the NTU Graduate Admissions AY2024-25 coursework fee PDF lists only MOE-subsidised programmes, and aggregators (libertify, collegedunia) quote only AY2026/AY2027 figures. Excludes miscellaneous fees (S$610 full-time for AY2025). Citizen/PR rates for the AY2026 and AY2027 intakes (added 2026-10-04 at the site owner's direction): the international total minus the S$5,000 NTU subsidy for Singaporeans and PRs in self-financed master's by coursework, deducted from the GST-inclusive total as for the AY2025 rows (AY2026: 56,156.80 - 5,000 = 51,156.80; AY2027: 58,403.07 - 5,000 = 53,403.07). Basis: NTU's Post-graduate Incentives page (linked from the EEE financial-matters page) describes the subsidy as continuing, with eligibility rules stated 'for students from AY2025 intake onwards' and no end date. Note that the page's subsidy sentences name only the 2024 and 2025 academic years explicitly, and the EEE MSc brochure of 10 Sep 2026 lists a single AY2027 fee without mentioning the subsidy, so confirm with eee_mscadmission@ntu.edu.sg before relying on the Citizen/PR figure.

programmes.name: MSc (Civil Engineering) (School of Civil and Environmental Engineering)
programmes.summary: Total tuition for the one-year programme, one fee for Citizens, PRs and international students, including 9% GST. No government subsidy for this intake. Miscellaneous fees are extra.
programmes.notes: Full-time normal candidature 1 year (2 semesters), 30 AUs; a part-time track also exists. This was NTU's MOE-subsidised engineering master's by coursework: the CEE programme page states MOE subsidy remains available to Singaporeans/PRs in the AY2024 intake but 'will not be available from AY2025 onwards', so all students admitted from AY2025 pay the non-subsidised fee. Current figures: 'Tuition fee for AY2026-2027 (based on minimum candidature)' S$57,232 full-time, incl. prevailing 9% GST, one fee for all nationalities, so the same figure is recorded under all three tiers; no SC/PR subsidy is stated for the AY2026 intake (the NTU Graduate Admissions financial-matters page states the S$5,000 self-financed-master's subsidy only for the academic years starting in 2024 and 2025). History: 2025 intake from the same page, 'Tuition fee for AY2025-2026' S$55,030.78 incl. GST for all nationalities (international row); the 2025 citizen and PR rows are DERIVED as S$55,030.78 minus the S$5,000 NTU subsidy for Singaporeans and PRs enrolling in self-financed master's by coursework programmes, which the NTU Graduate Admissions financial-matters page states applies 'for academic year starting in 2025' = S$50,030.78 (deducted from the GST-inclusive total; the page does not say whether it is applied before GST). 2024 intake (MOE-subsidised) from the NTU Graduate Admissions 'Tuition Fees for Graduate (Coursework)' AY2026-2027 PDF, table B1.3a (Full-Time Students Admitted in AY2024-2025, School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, M.Sc. (Civil Eng.)): Singapore Citizen S$9,750 and PR S$17,400 per academic year, subsidised, excl. GST (GST borne by MOE); the subsidised international fee is 'N.A.', so the 2024 international row is the non-subsidised fee S$48,940 incl. 9% GST. Excludes miscellaneous fees.

programmes.name: MSc in Artificial Intelligence (MSAI)
programmes.summary: Total tuition for the one-year programme, including 9% GST. Citizen/PR figure is the international fee less a S$5,000 NTU subsidy and a S$5,000 school study grant. Miscellaneous fees are extra.
programmes.notes: Self-financed programme, not MOE-subsidised. Total tuition incl. 9% GST for AY2027/28 and after: S$65,748.80 (12 months minimum full-time), published as a single figure for all nationalities; the international tier is that figure. NTU publishes no net Singapore Citizen/PR fee (checked 2026-10-01: the programme page, its FAQ, the CCDS MSc tuition-fee schedule PDF and the NTU Graduate Admissions AY2026-27 coursework fee PDF, which lists only MOE-subsidised programmes). The citizen and pr tiers are DERIVED: S$65,748.80 total minus the S$5,000 NTU subsidy the page states for 'Singaporeans and permanent residents who enrol in self-financed master's by coursework programmes at NTU' (section 'Financial Assistance (AY2025 intake onwards)') minus the additional S$5,000 CCDS study grant the page states for 'all Singaporeans and permanent residents' 'starting from AY2026 intake' = S$55,748.80. The page does not say whether these are applied before or after GST, so they are deducted from the GST-inclusive total. Excludes the means-tested top-up (up to S$15,000 for those needing financial aid) and the 10% NTU alumni rebate. History from the official CCDS MSc tuition-fee schedule PDF linked from the page ('Past Tuition Fees'): AY2025 and AY2026 intakes S$63,220 (all nationalities, incl. 9% GST); the SC/PR history rows for those intakes are derived the same way from that PDF, which states the S$5,000 NTU subsidy 'from AY2025 onwards' for SC and PR, the S$5,000 CCDS study grant for Singaporeans 'starting from AY2025 intake' and for PRs 'starting from AY2026 intake': AY2026 SC and PR S$63,220 - 5,000 - 5,000 = S$53,220; AY2025 SC S$53,220, PR S$63,220 - 5,000 = S$58,220. AY2024 intake had separate published rates, SC S$39,785, PR S$47,415, international S$59,187 (all incl. 9% GST). Excludes miscellaneous fees.

programmes.name: Nanyang MBA (full-time)
programmes.summary: Total fee for the 12-month programme, including 9% GST. Citizens and PRs get a 10% study grant off the published fee. Excludes the application fee and miscellaneous fees.
programmes.notes: Self-financed programme, not MOE-subsidised. 12-month (3-trimester) full-time programme, so the programme fee is the annual fee. Current figures are for the AY2027 (July 2027) intake from the Nanyang Business School admissions page's 'Fees & Funding' table: Nanyang MBA tuition S$85,280, which the page says excludes the prevailing 9% GST; S$85,280 x 1.09 = S$92,955.20 incl. GST, the total also shown on NBS's Fees & Funding fee schedule (ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/nanyang-mba/admissions/fees-funding: enrolment fee S$21,800 + instalments S$9,184.34 + S$30,985.43 + S$30,985.43). One fee for all nationalities, so the international tier is that figure. Citizen/PR DERIVED: the NBS Fees & Funding page states that Singapore Citizens and PRs admitted to the full-time Nanyang MBA get a study grant of 10% of the tuition fee, so the SC/PR figure is 90% of the published fee: S$92,955.20 x 0.9 = S$83,659.68 incl. GST (equivalently S$85,280 - S$8,528, plus 9% GST). History: 2026 intake from NTU's programme page (ntu.edu.sg/education/graduate-programme/nanyang-mba), 'Programme Fee (2026 Intake): S$89,380.00 (inclusive of 9% GST)', SC/PR 90% = S$80,442. 2024 intake (August 2024) from Wayback Machine captures of NBS's own pages: the admissions page captured 9 Jul 2024 (timestamp 20240709150834) lists 'AY2024 (August 2024 intake) ... Nanyang MBA ... S$ 75,000*' with '*Published tuition fee excludes prevailing GST set at 9%', and the Fees & Funding page captured 25 Jun 2024 (timestamp 20240625211650) gives the GST-inclusive fee schedule (enrolment fee S$21,800 + S$5,450 + S$27,250 + S$27,250 = S$81,750, 'includes prevailing GST rate') and the same 10% SC/PR study grant, so the 2024 international row is S$81,750 and the 2024 citizen/pr rows are DERIVED as 90% = S$73,575. 2025 intake (August 2025) added 2026-10-04 from the Wayback Machine capture of NBS's admissions page dated 9 Dec 2025 (timestamp 20251209043701, read through the translate.goog mirror of web.archive.org): 'AY2025 (August 2025 intake) ... Nanyang MBA, 12 months, Singapore, S$ 82,000' with '*Published tuition fee excludes prevailing GST set at 9%', so the 2025 international row is S$82,000 x 1.09 = S$89,380 incl. GST (the same total NBS's Fees & Funding schedule shows for the AY2026 intake, capture 20260418074853: enrolment fee S$21,800 + S$7,994.06 + S$29,792.97 + S$29,792.97 = S$89,380; the admissions page still showed the AY2024 table in its 27 May and 15 Jun and 8 Sep 2025 captures, and NTU's programme page went from 'Academic Year 2024: S$81,750' in its Jan-Jul 2025 captures to '2026 Intake: S$89,380' by Oct 2025 without ever printing a 2025 label). The 2025 citizen/pr rows are DERIVED as 90% = S$80,442, applying the 10% study grant for Singapore Citizens/PRs on the full-time Nanyang MBA that NBS's Fees & Funding page states in its 25 Jun 2024 capture and its Apr 2026 capture ('Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents of Singapore admitted to the full-time Nanyang MBA are eligible for a study grant of 10% of the tuition fees'); that page has no 2025 capture and the Dec 2025 admissions page does not mention the grant, so the 2025 SC/PR rows assume the grant ran unchanged between those two captures. Excludes the 10% NTU alumni grant, the S$100 application fee, the Student Services Fee and the one-time miscellaneous fee of S$620 incl. GST.

Figures are the 'Tuition Fees per Academic Year' for full-time students admitted in AY2026-2027 from NTU's official 'Tuition Fees for Graduate (Coursework)' PDF (table B1.1a, S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies row, which covers the M.Sc. in Asian Studies, International Political Economy, International Relations and Strategic Studies). Full-time candidature is normally one year (three trimesters), so the annual fee is the programme fee; RSIS's own site (rsis.edu.sg) blocks automated access, so the duration was not re-read from it. History (same PDF, tables B1.2a and B1.3a): AY2025-2026 and AY2024-2025 full-time admits had the same rates. Excludes miscellaneous fees.

programmes.name: MSc in Analytics (School of Physical and Mathematical Sciences)
programmes.summary: Total fee for the one-year programme, including 9% GST. Citizens get a S$10,900 study grant and PRs S$5,450 off the published fee. Miscellaneous and application fees are extra.
programmes.notes: Self-financed programme (listed under NTU's non-subsidised coursework programmes). One-year full-time programme taught over three trimesters, so the total programme fee is the annual fee (divided by durationYears 1). The SPMS programme page publishes one tuition fee for all nationalities per intake, incl. 9% GST: AY2027/28 S$64,841.92; AY2026/27 S$62,348.00; AY2025/26 S$59,950.00; the international tier is that figure. Citizen/PR DERIVED (re-verified 2026-10-01): the same page's 'Financial Assistance' section states that Singapore Citizens enjoy a study grant of S$10,000 + prevailing GST (S$10,900) and Singapore PRs S$5,000 + prevailing GST (S$5,450), applied evenly across the trimesters, so the current (AY2027/28) tiers are S$64,841.92 - S$10,900 = S$53,941.92 for citizens and S$64,841.92 - S$5,450 = S$59,391.92 for PRs (both incl. GST). The grant statement carries no intake year and the page says grants are reviewed annually, so it is applied only to the current published fee; the 2026 and 2025 history rows for citizens and PRs record the published total for everyone, not a derived net fee. AY2024 intake (added 2026-10-02) from the Wayback Machine capture of this page dated 21 Jul 2024 (timestamp 20240721112827): 'The tuition fees for Academic Year 2024/25 are as follows: Tuition Fee (inclusive of GST) S$55,000 + prevailing GST (S$ 59,950)' (international row); that capture also gave a payment schedule by nationality for AY2024/25 (deposit S$5,450 + first payment S$24,525 for all, then second payment S$19,075 for Singapore Citizens, S$24,525 for PRs and S$29,975 for international students, i.e. the SC S$10,900 and PR S$5,450 study grants already applied), so the 2024 citizen row is S$49,050 and the pr row S$54,500, the totals of that schedule. Excludes the means-tested financial aid (up to S$10,900 more for needy SC/PRs), the 10% NTU alumni grant, the S$50 application fee and the yearly one-time miscellaneous fee.
